body:
You can treat this as an advisory. The gist of my remarks are for enriching the reading experience pertaining to the references at the end of the page.

In https://github.com/OWASP/ASVS/blob/master/5.0/en/0x10-V1-Encoding-and-Sanitization.md, towards the end of the requirements, since we give quite some useful references from OWASP, one could also consider to add these:

- OWASP Input Validation Cheat Sheet (https://cheatsheetseries.owasp.org/cheatsheets/Input_Validation_Cheat_Sheet.html)
- OWASP Output Encoding Cheat Sheet (https://cheatsheetseries.owasp.org/cheatsheets/Output_Encoding_Cheat_Sheet.html)
- OWASP Server-Side Request Forgery Prevention Cheat Sheet 
- OWASP Server-Side Request Forgery Prevention Cheat Sheet (https://cheatsheetseries.owasp.org/cheatsheets/Server_Side_Request_Forgery_Prevention_Cheat_Sheet.html)
- OWASP Injection Prevention Cheat Sheet(https://cheatsheetseries.owasp.org/cheatsheets/Injection_Prevention_Cheat_Sheet.html)**
- OWASP SQL Injection Prevention Cheat Sheet (https://cheatsheetseries.owasp.org/cheatsheets/SQL_Injection_Prevention_Cheat_Sheet.html)

In addition, you could consider to rename
"OWASP Testing Guide 4.0: Client-Side Testing" to "Web Application Security Testing" and then change the hyperlink to https://owasp.org/www-project-web-security-testing-guide/latest/4-Web_Application_Security_Testing/. The reason for the is because it also then references to Input Validation testing (4.7) which could be very important reference for this section.

I also could suggest to refrain from references to a particular programming langauge. I am point to the reference of https://owasp.org/www-project-java-encoder/ which is Java focussed and probably could be considered for removal.

comments.body: Made a couple of changes but for the most part don't want to change too much, thanks

I understand that we want to release 5.0 on Friday, the changes cited in the ticket raised are not blocking the release, so these could be opted to be implemented after 5.0 release on Friday. While the references could be seen as a stretch, in my opinion these are very important for entry level users of ASVS and will bring the practical (than academic) side of ASVS. With the changes you have done, I see that we will still miss some of the good OWASP references.  Once again, thanks for your work.
